title: Ashenmere Metro System
notebook: Metro: forty-five million ₭ over sixteen weeks for three underground lines and eighteen stations.
Eighty thousand commuters a day on streets laid out for carriages. Vostane's concern is procurement.
Lucan Vael's Thornfeld Valley Development Corporation has already expressed interest in the contracts.

narrative.text: Ashenmere's streets were laid out in the eighteenth century for horses and carriages. They now carry eighty thousand commuters daily on roads that were not designed for automobiles, in a city whose population has doubled since 1940. The proposed metro system — three underground lines, eighteen stations, connecting the government district, industrial zones, and residential quarters — would be the largest urban infrastructure project in Veltrian history. It would transform how the capital moves.

Forty-five million ₭ over sixteen weeks. This is the most expensive single project this government will consider. The economic impact is substantial — reduced congestion increases productivity, metro stations become commercial hubs, and the construction itself employs three thousand workers. The concern is procurement. A project this large involves major construction contracts, and the Thornfeld Valley Development Corporation — Lucan Vael's company — has already expressed interest. How we award these contracts will define whether this is a clean infrastructure investment or another chapter in the story of oligarchs and public money.

At week eight — the midpoint — the project reaches the critical contracting decision: open competitive international bidding, award to Vael's company, or form a domestic consortium of multiple Veltrian firms.

choices.text: "Approve the metro system. Forty-five million ₭ from infrastructure and urban development funds. Vostane, I want the procurement process designed before we break ground — transparent, competitive, auditable. The size of the contracts will attract every oligarch in the country. We are going to make sure the public gets value for its money, not just the well-connected. The capital deserves a modern transit system. It will get one — built clean."

"Defer the metro for one budget cycle. The concept is sound, but forty-five million ₭ requires fiscal conditions that are more stable than what we currently have. Vostane, continue the engineering studies and prepare the procurement framework. When the deficit improves, we will break ground. This is a deferral, not a rejection."

"Forty-five million ₭ for an underground rail system is an indulgence the country cannot afford. Ashenmere's surface transportation — buses, trams, the existing road network — will be upgraded incrementally. The metro is a prestige project dressed as infrastructure. When the national debt is under control and the Tyvaren situation is resolved, we can discuss urban transit. Until then, the answer is no."
